requirement: The toolchain must be written in Python, and uv must manage the Python project.
The toolchain must install as one Python package that supplies the command `dsml`.
The toolchain must run on the operating systems that decision record 03 gives.
Validation, code generation and traceability must not use an AI model.
Validation, code generation and trace reports must not use the network. Only the local OpenSysML child process is permitted.
The toolchain must not write a secret value to a log, a report or a generated file.
Each dependency of the toolchain and of the generated code must have a license that the company accepts for internal software.
Generated code must pin each dependency to the exact version that the version baseline gives.
The PRD set and the user documentation of the toolchain must use ASD-STE100 Issue 9.
Each PRD requirement must have a unique ID with the prefix of its PRD.
The DSML appendix must contain each PRD requirement. OpenSysML must parse the appendix with no error.
Validation and code generation of a model with 1,000 elements must finish in the time that decision record 03 gives.
The DSML must be a SysML v2 model library package with the name `DSML`.
The DSML must extend SysML v2 only with metadata definitions, attribute definitions and enumeration definitions. It must not add a concrete syntax.
Each DSML element kind must be available as a user-defined keyword, for example `#Need`, `#Entity` and `#ContainerService`.
OpenSysML must parse and resolve the DSML library with no error and no warning.
The DSML library must use only SysML v2 constructs that the OMG pilot implementation also accepts.
The toolchain package must include the DSML library, so a model needs no download.
A model must be a set of `.sysml` files in one Git repository. The toolchain configuration file must give the files or folders of the model.
A model must import the DSML library with `private import DSML::*;` or refer to its elements with qualified names.

Each DSML keyword of an element kind must be a metadata definition that specializes `Metaobjects::SemanticMetadata`. Its base type must hold the attributes of the element kind. A keyword on a dependency, and a metadata definition that holds its own attributes, must be a plain metadata definition.
The model must give attribute values with redefinitions of the base type features, for example `:>> priority = Priority::must;`.
A stakeholder must be a part definition with the keyword `#Stakeholder`.
A need must be a concern usage with the keyword `#Need`. It must have one or more `stakeholder` members that refer to a stakeholder.
A need must have these attributes: ID (the short name), `title`, text (the `doc` comment), `priority` and `status`.
A requirement must be a requirement usage with the keyword `#Requirement`. It can frame one or more needs with `frame`.
A requirement must have these attributes: ID (the short name), `title`, text (the `doc` comment), `kind`, `priority` and `status`. It can also have `rationale`, `source` and `owner`.

The DSML must define these enumerations. `Priority`: `must`, `should`, `could`, `wont`. `Status`: `draft`, `approved`, `implemented`, `verified`, `retired`. `RequirementKind`: `functional`, `performance`, `security`, `interface`, `constraint`.

A requirement derivation must use the `#derivation` connection of the SysML v2 `RequirementDerivation` library. A refinement must use a dependency with the `#refinement` metadata of the SysML v2 `ModelingMetadata` library.
A requirement can contain formal constraints (`require constraint`) that refer to attributes of model elements. Quantities must use the SysML v2 quantity and unit libraries.
A project can add attributes to needs and requirements with a project library that specializes the DSML base types.
An application must be a part usage with the keyword `#Application`. Its attribute `target` must have one of the values `fastapi`, `react` or `nextjs`.
A model can contain more than one application.
An entity must be a part definition with the keyword `#Entity`. Each attribute usage of an entity is a field.

A field type must be one of: `String`, `Integer`, `Boolean`, `Real` from the SysML v2 libraries; `Decimal`, `Date`, `DateTime` and `Uuid` from the DSML library; or an enumeration definition in the model.
An entity must have one primary key field with the keyword `#Key`.

A field multiplicity of `[1]` must mean a required field, and `[0..1]` an optional field. A field can have these DSML constraints: `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minValue`, `maxValue`, `pattern`, `unique`, and `precision` and `scale` for a `Decimal` field.
A relation between entities must be a reference usage typed by the related entity, with the multiplicity `[0..1]`, `[1]` or `[*]`. A relation with `[*]` at the two ends is a many-to-many relation.
An application must expose an entity with an entity usage that has the keyword `#Exposed`. Its attribute `crud` must list the CRUD operations: `create`, `read`, `update`, `delete` and `list`.
A custom operation must be an action definition with the keyword `#Operation` and typed `in` and `out` parameters. The toolchain must not read the body of the action.
Each operation must have an HTTP method and a path. The DSML must give defaults for CRUD operations. A custom operation must state its method and path.
A `react` application must refer to the application whose API it calls, with a dependency that has the `#Calls` metadata. The two applications then use one API model.

Phase 2: a view must be a part usage in an application with the keyword `#View`. Its attribute `kind` must be `list`, `detail` or `form`. A list or detail view must refer to one entity. A form view must refer to one operation.
Phase 2: an application can give its navigation as an ordered list of views.

The roles of a model must be the values of one enumeration definition with the keyword `#Roles`. Each exposed operation, entity and view must list the roles that can use it in its attribute `allowedRoles`. The attribute value `public = true` must mean that no authentication is necessary.
A destructive database change must have the `#Destructive` metadata on the changed entity or field. A rename must give the old name in the attribute `renamedFrom`.
A logical infrastructure element must be a part usage with one of the logical kinds in the table of the section "Infrastructure layer".
A logical element must not contain an AWS term, an AWS attribute or an AWS service name.
Each logical element must have one AWS realization: a part usage with the matching AWS kind and a dependency with the `#Realizes` metadata to the logical element.
An AWS realization must hold the AWS attributes, for example the RDS instance class or the Fargate CPU and memory.

Each application must be allocated to one logical element with `allocate`. A `fastapi` or `nextjs` application must be allocated to a `#ContainerService`. A `react` application must be allocated to a `#StaticSite`.
A container service or a static site must refer to each database, user directory and secret store that it uses, with a dependency that has the `#Uses` metadata.

An environment must be a part usage with the keyword `#Environment`. It must have an AWS account ID, an AWS Region and a domain name. The model must contain the environments `dev`, `staging` and `prod`.
An environment can change only these attributes of an AWS realization: `cpu`, `memory`, `instanceClass`, `desiredCount`, `minCount`, `maxCount`, `multiAz` and `natGatewayCount`.
The model must have one part usage with the keyword `#ToolingAccount`. It must have the AWS account ID and the AWS Region of the ECR repositories.
A project must not add a logical kind or an AWS kind. A new kind must come in a new version of the DSML library.
A verification must be a verification usage with the keyword `#Verification`. It must have an ID (the short name), a `title` and a `method`.
The attribute `method` must have one of the values `test`, `analysis`, `inspection` or `demonstration`.
A verification must refer to each requirement that it verifies with `verify` in its objective.
A verification with the method `test` must give one or more test file paths, relative to the repository root, in the attribute `testFiles`.
A verification can give test case names in the attribute `testCases`, for example a pytest node ID.
Each need, requirement and verification must have a short name with the pattern of its kind: `N-<NNN>`, `R-<NNN>` or `V-<NNN>`. `<NNN>` has three or more digits with leading zeros.
A project can set different ID patterns in the toolchain configuration file.
Each short name must be unique in the model. A deleted ID must not be used again.
Each element without a short name must use its qualified name as its identity.
An element can have an OpenSysML `IdentityMetadata::ElementId` annotation. The DSML must not require it.
A waiver must be a `#Waiver` metadata usage on the element. It must have the attributes `rule` (the rule ID), `reason` and `owner`. It can have the attribute `expires` (a date).
The DSML library must have a semantic version. Each model must state the major and minor version of the library that it uses, with the `#DsmlVersion` metadata on its root package.
A minor version of the DSML library must not make a valid model invalid. A major version must come with migration notes.
The command `dsml` must have the seven subcommands `init`, `validate`, `generate`, `trace`, `ir`, `check-output` and `version`, with the options in the table of the section "Command line interface".
Each subcommand must stop with exit code 0 if it finds no error, 1 if it finds an error finding or a `--check` difference, and 2 if a usage error or an internal error occurs.
`dsml generate` must validate the model first. If there is an error finding, it must stop and write no file.
`dsml generate --check` must write no file. It must list each file that a normal run would add, change or delete.
`dsml generate` must generate only one part of the output when the user gives `--application <name>`, `--infrastructure` or `--pipelines`.
Each subcommand must write its report to standard output, or to the file that `--output` gives.
A message about a model location must give the file path, the line and the column.
Messages to the user must use ASD-STE100 Issue 9.
A subcommand must not ask for input from a terminal.
The option `--verbose` must write debug messages to standard error.

`dsml check-output` must run `tsc`, `ruff`, `tofu validate`, `tflint` and the FSD linter Steiger on the generated code of the selected targets. It must report a missing tool as an error with the tool name.
The toolchain must read its configuration from `dsml.toml` in the repository root, or from the file that the option `--config` gives.

The configuration file must give: the model files or folders; the output folder of each application, of the infrastructure and of the pipelines; the ID patterns; the optional rule sets; the default trace baseline; and the IaC options for one tool only.
The configuration file must have a schema version. The toolchain must report an unknown key or an unknown schema version as an error.
Environment variables, the user name, the host name, the locale, the time zone and the clock must not change the generated output.
The configuration file must not contain secret values.
The toolchain must call OpenSysML through the `opensysml` Python client. The client must start `sysml-grpc` as a private child process.
The toolchain must pin one OpenSysML version for the Python package and the `sysml-grpc` binary. The version must come from the version baseline.
At start, the toolchain must compare the version of `sysml-grpc` with the pinned version. If they are different, it must stop with exit code 2.
Only the IR adapter module must import the `opensysml` package. A lint rule in the toolchain CI must enforce this.
The adapter must convert each OpenSysML diagnostic into a finding of the category SYN of the validation PRD.
The IR must be JSON. The toolchain package must contain the JSON Schema of the IR.
The IR must have a semantic version in the field `irVersion`. A change that removes or renames a field must increase the major version.
The IR must hold each element of the five layers, its DSML attributes, its trace links and its source location (file, line, column).
The IR must not contain an OpenSysML type, an OpenSysML object or an OpenSysML internal ID.
Validators and generators must read only the IR. They get the results of formal constraints from the IR (PRD-CORE-054), not from OpenSysML.
The toolchain CI must compare the IR of each reference model with a stored golden IR file. A change of the OpenSysML version must pass this comparison before a release.

The adapter must evaluate each formal constraint of a requirement through OpenSysML, one time for each environment, and write each result into the IR. The evaluation uses the attribute values of that environment. A result is `true`, `false` or `unknown`. An `unknown` result gives the features that have no value.
The same model, configuration file and toolchain version must give byte-identical generated files, IR, reports and trace manifests on each supported operating system.
The toolchain CI must run each reference model on Linux x64, and compare the outputs byte by byte with the golden files.
The toolchain CI must compare the output of each reference model with stored golden files.
Generators must write each list in an output file in a defined order: by element identity, then by name.
The output must not depend on the order of the model files on disk or in the configuration file.
The output must not contain a timestamp, a random value, an absolute path, a user name or a host name.
Each output file must use UTF-8 with no byte order mark, LF line ends and one LF at the end of the file.

Templates must give their output in the format of the pinned formatter for the file type: Prettier for TypeScript, `ruff format` for Python, `tofu fmt` for HCL. The generator must not run a formatter. The toolchain CI must run each formatter in check mode on the golden files and find no change.
The generator must not write lockfiles (`uv.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.terraform.lock.hcl`). The generated CI makes them, and Git keeps them.
A minor or patch release of the toolchain must not change the output for an unchanged model, except to fix a defect that its release notes name.
The header of a generated file must give the major version of the toolchain only.

A generated file must have a name that ends with `.gen.<ext>` or `_gen.py`, or be on the fixed-name list of its target. Each generation PRD gives its fixed-name list, for example `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `Dockerfile` and the Next.js `app/` folder.
The generator must keep a manifest in `.dsml/generated.json`. For each generated file, it must give the path and the SHA-256 hash. For each create-once file, it must give the path.
At each run, the generator must delete each generated file of the old manifest that the new run does not write.
The generator must not write, change or delete a file that is not a generated file of the old or new manifest, except a new create-once file.
If the hash of a generated file is different from its hash in the manifest, `dsml generate` must stop with an error that lists the changed files. The option `--overwrite` must replace them.
The generator must write a create-once file only if no file exists at its path.
Generated code must call hand-written code through a typed interface, for example a handler function with typed parameters. A difference between the two must cause a type check error.
The generator must own the dependency lists of each target. A developer must add a dependency in the configuration file, not in a generated file.
The toolchain must be a Python package that uv builds. The release process must publish it to the internal package index. A user must be able to install it with `uv tool install`.
The package must contain the DSML library, the IR schema, the templates and the pinned copy of the shadcn/ui components.
The installation must supply the `sysml-grpc` binary of the pinned OpenSysML version and check its SHA-256 hash against the release checksums of OpenSysML.
The toolchain must supply a GitHub Action that installs a pinned toolchain version and runs one subcommand.
When its input `sarif` is `true`, the GitHub Action must upload the SARIF findings to GitHub code scanning.
Toolchain releases must use semantic versioning. The release notes must name each change to the generated output.
Before each release, the toolchain CI must generate and deploy each reference model to a sandbox AWS account, and remove it after the test.
Each application generator must read only the IR.
For each application in the IR, the generator of its target must write the code in the output folder that the configuration file gives for that application.
A generator must write code only for the entities, operations, views and roles in the IR, and for the health endpoint of PRD-APP-012.
A FastAPI or Next.js application must also write an OpenAPI 3.1 document, `openapi.gen.json`, from the IR. The OpenAPI document that the running service supplies must agree with it.

The client types of a React application and the schemas of the API that it calls must come from the same IR entities and operations. A contract test in the toolchain CI must compare the generated client with the `openapi.gen.json` of the called application.
Phase 2: a React application can call an external API that an imported OpenAPI file gives, in place of an application in the model.
Each application must authenticate users with the Amazon Cognito user pool of its environment. Web clients must use Cognito managed login with the authorization code flow and PKCE.

For each operation, the generated server code must examine the access token. It must return HTTP 401 if there is no valid token, and HTTP 403 if no group in the `cognito:groups` claim is in `allowedRoles`. An operation with `public = true` must need no token.

The generated web client must show only the navigation items and views that the roles of the user permit. It must send a user with no session to the login page. The server check of PRD-APP-008 stays the protection.
Each application must read its environment values at run time, not at build time. One build or one container image must operate in all environments.
Each application must get secret values from environment variables that ECS sets from Secrets Manager. Generated code must not contain a secret value.
A FastAPI or Next.js application must supply `GET /healthz` with no authentication. It must return HTTP 200 while the process operates.

The Dockerfile of a FastAPI or Next.js application must use a multi-stage build and a base image pinned by digest. The container must run as a user that is not root and must not contain a secret value.
API errors must use problem details (RFC 9457) with the media type `application/problem+json`.
Server logs must be JSON lines on standard output, with a request ID in each line. Logs must not contain tokens or secret values.
The generated code of each target must pass `dsml check-output` with no error.
Each generated source file must have the trace header that the traceability PRD gives.
The FastAPI target must use Python, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic and pytest, and uv must manage the project. The versions must come from the version baseline.
The generator must write one slice folder for each operation: `app/features/<entity>/<operation>/`. A slice must contain `endpoint_gen.py` (the router) and `schemas_gen.py` (the Pydantic models).
For a CRUD operation, the generator must write the handler as `handler_gen.py`. For a custom operation, it must write `handler.py` as a create-once stub.
Code that all slices use must be in `app/shared/`: the database session, the SQLAlchemy models, the Cognito token check, the configuration and the error types.
`app/main_gen.py` must create the FastAPI application and register the router of each slice in sorted order.
A generated file in a slice must import only from its own slice and from `app/shared/`.

Each operation in the IR must have one endpoint with the HTTP method and the path of the operation. CRUD operations must use the default methods and paths in the table of the section "API operations and schemas" unless the model gives a different method or path.

For each exposed entity, the generator must write Pydantic v2 models for create input, update input and output. The key field must not be in the create input. Each field of the update input must be optional.
Field rules must become Pydantic field constraints: `minLength` and `maxLength` to `min_length` and `max_length`, `minValue` and `maxValue` to `ge` and `le`, and `pattern` to `pattern`.
A request that breaks a field rule must get HTTP 422. A request that breaks a `unique` rule must get HTTP 409. A request for an entity that does not exist must get HTTP 404.
A `list` operation must accept `limit` (default 50, maximum 200) and `offset` (default 0). It must return the found entities in `items`, sorted by key, and their count in `total`.
An output schema must give a related entity as its key, not as a nested object.

For a custom operation, the generated endpoint must validate the input, check the roles, open a database session and then call `handle(input, session, user)` in `handler.py`. It must return the output that `handle` gives as the output schema.
The create-once `handler.py` stub must contain the typed `handle` function. Its body must raise `NotImplementedError`, so the endpoint returns HTTP 501 until a developer writes the logic.
For each entity, the generator must write one typed SQLAlchemy 2 model in `app/shared/db/models/<entity>_gen.py`. The table name must be the entity name in snake case.
Field types must map to PostgreSQL types as the table of the section "Data access and migrations" gives.
A `[*]` to `[*]` relation must have a generated join table. A `[0..1]` or `[1]` relation must have a foreign key.
Database access must use the SQLAlchemy mode and the database driver that decision record 03 gives.

The generator must keep the schema snapshot in `.dsml/schema-snapshot.json`. If the IR schema is different from the snapshot, the generator must write one new Alembic migration and then update the snapshot.
A migration file must have the name `migrations/versions/<NNNN>_<slug>_gen.py`. Its revision ID must come from its content and its number, not from a random value or the clock.
The generator must keep each migration file that it wrote before, byte for byte.
The generator must not write a migration that drops or renames a table or a column, unless the IR has the `#Destructive` metadata for that change.
`app/migrate_gen.py` must apply all migrations that the database does not have, and then stop. The deployment runs it as decision record 03 gives.

`app/shared/auth/cognito_gen.py` must supply a FastAPI dependency. It must check the signature of the access token against the JWKS of the user pool, and the claims `iss`, `token_use` (`access`), `client_id` and `exp`.
The dependency must keep the JWKS in memory and get it again only when a token has an unknown key ID.
`app/shared/config_gen.py` must read the configuration from environment variables at start. If a mandatory variable is missing, the application must stop with a message that names the variable.
The Dockerfile must install the locked dependencies with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` and run Uvicorn on port 8000.
The fixed-name generated files of the FastAPI target must be: `pyproject.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `alembic.ini`, `migrations/env.py` and each `__init__.py` in a generated folder.
`pytest` must run on the generated project with no error when the project has no tests.

The React target must use strict TypeScript, pnpm, Vite, React, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, TanStack Form, Zod, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui and Amplify Auth. The versions must come from the version baseline.
The generator must put the code in the FSD layers `app`, `pages`, `widgets`, `features`, `entities` and `shared` in `src/`.
Generated code must obey the FSD import rules: a module imports only from lower layers, and only through the public API of a slice.
Each slice must have a create-once `index.ts` that re-exports the generated `index.gen.ts`.
The path alias `@/` must refer to `src/`.
Slice names and file names must be the kebab case of the model element names.

section: Map from model elements to FSD layers
requirement: The generator must put each model element in the slice and the files that the table of the section "Map from model elements to FSD layers" gives.

section: Map from model elements to FSD layers
requirement: The Zod schemas of an entity must apply the same field rules as the Pydantic models of PRD-APP-112.

section: Map from model elements to FSD layers
requirement: The generator must write the shadcn/ui components that the templates use into `shared/ui` as create-once files, from the pinned copy in the toolchain package.
The generator must write the TanStack Router route tree with code-based routing in `src/app/router/routes.gen.tsx`. The project must not use the TanStack Router file-based routing plugin.
Each view must have one route. A list view must use the path `/<entities>`, a detail view `/<entities>/$id`, and a form view `/<operation>`.
The `beforeLoad` function of each route must check the session and the roles of the view. With no session, it must start the login. With no permitted role, it must show a "not permitted" page.
The loader of each list and detail route must load its data with `queryClient.ensureQueryData` and the query options of the entity slice.
Each query key must be an array in the form `[<entity>, <operation>, <parameters>]`.
After a mutation, the generated code must invalidate the queries of the changed entity.
Each form must use TanStack Form with the Zod schema of its operation as the validator. Each field must use the shadcn/ui form components, with a label and an error message.
The client must show a problem details response as an error message with its `title` and `detail`.
Each table must have column headers, and the user must be able to reach each control with the keyboard.
Before the first render, the application must read `/config.json`. The file must give the API base URL, the AWS Region, the user pool ID, the app client ID and the managed login domain.
`shared/auth/amplify.gen.ts` must configure Amplify Auth from the runtime configuration and use Cognito managed login with PKCE.
The API client must add the access token of the session to each request as a bearer token.
`pnpm build` must write the static files to `dist/`. The build must not contain environment values.
The generator must write a Steiger configuration, and `dsml check-output` must run Steiger with no error.
The fixed-name generated files of the React target must be: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`, `components.json` and `steiger.config.ts`.

The Next.js target must use strict TypeScript, pnpm, Next.js with the App Router, React, TanStack Query, TanStack Form, Zod, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM and Amplify Auth with its Next.js adapter. The versions must come from the version baseline.
The Next.js `app/` folder must be at the project root and hold only route files that re-export from `src/`. The generator must own the full `app/` folder.
The FSD layers must be in `src/`, and the layers `app` and `pages` must have the names `_app` and `_pages`.
The generator must map model elements to slices as PRD-APP-210 gives, with the layer names of PRD-APP-303.
A slice must export server-only modules through `index.server.ts` and other modules through `index.ts`. Each server-only module must import `server-only`.
The generated code must obey the FSD import rules of PRD-APP-203, and `dsml check-output` must run Steiger with no error.
For each operation, the generator must write a route handler in `src/_app/api-routes/<operation>.gen.ts`. A generated `app/api/<path>/route.ts` must re-export it.
The REST contract must be the contract of the FastAPI target (PRD-APP-110 to PRD-APP-115), with the path prefix `/api`.
A route handler must validate the input with the Zod schema of the operation, check the token and the roles, call the server function of the operation and return JSON or problem details.

For a CRUD operation, the generator must write the server function as `features/<operation>/api/<operation>.server.gen.ts`. For a custom operation, it must write `<operation>.server.ts` as a create-once stub that throws an error with the HTTP status 501.
Server components of pages must call the server functions for `read` and `list` directly, with no HTTP request. Client components must call the route handlers through TanStack Query.
For each view, the generator must write a page slice in `src/_pages/<view>` and a generated `app/<route>/page.tsx` that re-exports it. Routes must use the paths of PRD-APP-221.
Each form must be a client component that uses TanStack Form with the Zod schema of its operation. The route handler must validate the same input again with the same schema.
Authentication must use Amplify Auth with its Next.js adapter, and the adapter must keep the tokens in cookies.
The generated request interceptor (`middleware.ts` or `proxy.ts`, as the pinned Next.js version requires) must send a request for a protected page with no session to the login.
Server components and route handlers must get the session through the Amplify adapter and apply the role checks of PRD-APP-008.

The root layout must give the public runtime values (Region, user pool ID, app client ID, login domain) to client components from server-side environment variables. The build must not use `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables.
The generator must write the Drizzle schema of all entities in `src/shared/db/schema.gen.ts`, with the type map of PRD-APP-121.

The generator must write each migration from the difference between `.dsml/schema-snapshot.json` and the IR, in the file format that the Drizzle migrator reads. The project must not use `drizzle-kit generate`.
PRD-APP-125 to PRD-APP-128 must also apply to the Next.js target. The migration command must be `node migrate.gen.mjs`.
The Next.js build must use the `standalone` output. The Dockerfile must run the server on port 3000.

The fixed-name generated files of the Next.js target must be: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.ts`, the full `app/` folder, `middleware.ts` or `proxy.ts`, `drizzle.config.ts`, `components.json`, `steiger.config.ts`, `Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore`.
The generator must write the folders and root modules of the tree in the section "Output structure and tool compatibility" in the infrastructure output folder of the configuration file.
Each generated HCL file must have a name that ends with `.gen.tf`. A platform engineer can add hand-written `.tf` files to a root module, and the generator must not change them.
With the default configuration, the HCL must be valid for the pinned OpenTofu version and for the pinned Terraform version. The `required_version` constraint must accept the two pinned versions.

A feature of only one tool must be available only through an IaC option in the configuration file, for example OpenTofu state encryption. With such an option, the generator must write a comment that names the one tool that accepts the output.
Each root module must pin the AWS provider to the exact version of the version baseline.
Each root module must use the S3 backend with S3 native state locks (`use_lockfile = true`) and encryption. The state bucket must be in the AWS account of the root module.
The output must use only `aws_*` resources and data sources and local modules. It must not use a module from a registry or from a different repository.

HCL addresses must be the snake case of the element names. AWS resource names must have the form `<product>-<environment>-<element>`. If a name is longer than the AWS limit, the generator must shorten it and add a hash of the full name.
The image of each container service must be a root module variable `<application>_image_digest`. The CI/CD pipeline must give its value.

Each environment root module must output the values that the pipelines need: the ECS cluster and service names, the API URL, the Cognito user pool ID, app client IDs and login domain, and, in phase 2, the S3 bucket and the CloudFront distribution ID.
Network: the module must write a VPC with a public and a private subnet in each of two or more availability zones, an internet gateway, and the number of NAT gateways that `natGatewayCount` gives.

Container service: the module must write an ECS cluster, a Fargate service and a task definition with the `cpu`, `memory` and `desiredCount` of the realization. Tasks must be in private subnets with no public IP address.
Container service: the module must write target tracking auto scaling on CPU, between `minCount` and `maxCount`.

Container service: the module must write an ALB in the public subnets with an HTTPS listener, an ACM certificate for the API domain, a redirect from HTTP to HTTPS, and a Route 53 record. The target group must use `/healthz` as the health check.

Container service: the task execution role must permit only image pulls from the tooling ECR repository, reads of the secrets that the service uses, and log writes. The task role must permit only access to the elements that the service uses (`#Uses`).
Container service: the module must write a CloudWatch log group with a retention of 30 days, and a second task definition that runs the migration command of the application.

Database: the module must write an RDS for PostgreSQL instance in private subnets with the `instanceClass` and `multiAz` of the realization, storage encryption with a KMS key, backups for 7 days, and a master password that RDS keeps in Secrets Manager. In prod, deletion protection must be on.
Database: its security group must permit port 5432 only from the security groups of the container services that use it.

User directory: the module must write one Cognito user pool, one app client for each application that uses it (no client secret, authorization code with PKCE, callback URLs on the environment domain), one group for each role value and a managed login domain. Self sign-up must be off.
Secret store: the module must write one Secrets Manager secret and one KMS key for each secret element. The HCL must not contain secret values.

Phase 2, static site: the module must write a private S3 bucket with versioning, a CloudFront distribution with origin access control, an ACM certificate in `us-east-1` and a Route 53 alias. CloudFront must return `/index.html` with HTTP 200 for paths that do not exist.

Tooling: the tooling root module must write one ECR repository for each container application, with immutable tags, scan on push and a lifecycle policy. The repository policy must permit pulls by the task execution roles of the environment accounts.

Container service: the ECS service must ignore changes to its task definition, because the pipeline sets it after the migrations. The service must use the ECS deployment circuit breaker with rollback.
Each environment root module must call the same local modules. Only the environment attributes of PRD-DSML-042 can make two environments different.
The AWS provider of each root module must set `allowed_account_ids` to the account ID of its environment or of the tooling account.
The generator must not create AWS accounts. The accounts and AWS Organizations must exist before the bootstrap.
The bootstrap root module of each account must write the state bucket (versioning, encryption, public access blocked), the GitHub OIDC identity provider and the IAM roles for CI.

Each environment account must have a plan role with read-only access, which pull requests can use, and a deploy role, which only the GitHub environment of that account can use. The trust policies must check the repository and the environment in the `sub` claim.
The tooling account must have a push role, which only workflows of the main branch and of release tags can use.
The bootstrap root module must start with local state. The generator must write a README that gives the command to move that state into the bucket that the module creates.
Each resource that stores data (S3, RDS, Secrets Manager, ECR) must have encryption at rest.
Only ALB listeners and CloudFront distributions can accept traffic from the internet. RDS must have `publicly_accessible = false`, and each S3 bucket must block public access.
A security group must not permit ingress from `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`, except an ALB security group on ports 80 and 443.
An IAM policy must not use the action `*` or a service wildcard such as `s3:*`. It can use the resource `*` only for actions that have no resource-level permissions in AWS.
Each HTTPS listener must use the TLS security policy that the version baseline gives.

The AWS provider of each root module must set `default_tags` with `dsml:product`, `dsml:environment` and `dsml:model-commit`. Each resource must add the tag `dsml:element` with the identity of its model element, and `dsml:application` where an application owns it.
The value of `dsml:model-commit` must come from the root module variable `model_commit` at plan time. Generated files must not contain the commit.
If a tag value is longer than the AWS limit of 256 characters, the generator must shorten it and add a hash of the full value.
`dsml check-output --infrastructure` must run `tofu fmt -check`, `tofu validate` (after `tofu init -backend=false`) and `tflint` with the AWS rule set on each root module.
The toolchain CI must also run `terraform validate` on the golden output of each reference model.
An IaC security scan of the golden output must find no finding with high or critical severity. The version baseline gives the scanner.
After an apply, a second `tofu plan` with the same model and the same commit must show no change.
The generator must write `.github/workflows/pr.gen.yml`, `main.gen.yml` and `promote.gen.yml` with the triggers and jobs in the table of the section "Workflows and jobs".
`pr.gen.yml` must run `dsml validate` and upload the SARIF findings to GitHub code scanning.
`pr.gen.yml` must run `dsml generate --check` and fail if a generated file is different from the committed file.

For each application, `pr.gen.yml` must install the dependencies from the committed lockfile (`uv sync --frozen` or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`), then run the linter, the type checker and the tests. A lockfile that does not agree with the dependency list must make the job fail.
`pr.gen.yml` must run `dsml check-output`.
`pr.gen.yml` must run `tofu plan` for dev with the plan role, and write the plan text in the job summary. It must not apply.
`main.gen.yml` must build each container image and the static files of each React application one time. It must then deploy them to dev.
`promote.gen.yml` must deploy the image digests and the static files of one main build to staging, then to prod. It must not build again.
Each deploy job must use a `concurrency` group for its environment, so only one deployment runs in an environment at a time. A new run must not cancel a running deployment.
Workflows must get AWS credentials only through GitHub OIDC and the roles of PRD-IAC-027 and PRD-IAC-028. They must not use long-term access keys.
Each job must declare the smallest `permissions` set that it needs. Only jobs that use AWS must have `id-token: write`.
Each deploy job must use the GitHub environment of its target environment (`dev`, `staging` or `prod`).
The generator must write a README with the settings that a repository administrator must make: the GitHub environments, required reviewers for `prod`, and branch protection for the main branch.
Each third-party action must be pinned to a full commit SHA from the version baseline, with its version in a comment.
Workflows must not write secret values to logs or job summaries. Values from AWS outputs that are not secret can appear in summaries.
A deploy job must run `tofu apply` with the image digests of the build and `model_commit` set to the commit of the build.

After the apply, the job must run the migration task definition of each application with a database as a one-off ECS task, and wait for it. If the task fails, the job must stop before it changes a service.
After the migrations, the job must set each ECS service to its new task definition and wait for a steady state. If the ECS deployment circuit breaker rolls back, the job must fail.
Phase 2: for each React application, the job must upload the static files to its S3 bucket, write `/config.json` from the outputs of the root module, and invalidate the CloudFront cache.
`promote.gen.yml` must deploy to prod only after the staging deployment of the same build succeeded and a required reviewer approved the `prod` environment.
Each deploy job must write a job summary with the environment, the image digests, the model commit and the applied migrations.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: Each rule must be Python code that reads only the IR. Each rule must have an ID, a category, a default severity, a message and a fix hint.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: Rule IDs must have the form `<CATEGORY>-<NNN>`. A deleted rule ID must not be used again.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The severities must be `error`, `warning` and `info`. A finding with the severity `error` must stop code generation.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The configuration file can increase the severity of a rule, or turn off a rule with the default severity `warning` or `info`. It must not decrease the severity of a rule with the default severity `error` or turn it off.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The option `--fail-on warning` must make `dsml validate` stop with exit code 1 if there is a warning.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The validator must write findings as text, as JSON, or as SARIF 2.1.0 with the rule metadata and the source locations.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The validator must sort findings by file, line, column and rule ID.

section: Rule engine, severities and output formats
requirement: The toolchain CI must have, for each rule, one model that the rule accepts and one model that the rule rejects.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: A `#Waiver` must stop the findings of its rule on its element only. The report must list waived findings in a separate group, and SARIF must give them as suppressions with the reason.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: After the `expires` date of a waiver, its findings must come back, and the validator must report rule `STR-014`.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: The identity rules (category IDN) must run only when the user gives `--baseline <git-ref>` or the configuration file gives a default baseline. The validator must read the baseline model from the local Git repository.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: The validator must read the result of each formal constraint for each environment from the IR (PRD-CORE-054). It reports rule `FCN-001` for a `false` result and rule `FCN-002` for an `unknown` result.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: The text rules (category TXT) must be off by default. The configuration file must be able to turn them on.

section: Waivers, baselines, formal constraints and text rules
requirement: The text rules must use the project dictionary of the top-level PRD as a list of additional approved words. The toolchain must not claim full STE compliance.
The validator must contain each rule in the catalog of the section "Rule catalog for phase 1", with its default severity.
The model must use these link types: the `stakeholder` member of a need, `frame`, `#derivation`, `#refinement`, `satisfy`, `allocate`, `#Realizes` and `verify`.
A `satisfy` link can come from an application element or from an infrastructure element.
The IR must hold each link with its type and the identities of its source and target.
The traceability engine must follow links in the two directions: from a need to its code, tests and AWS resources, and from a file or resource back to its needs.

section: Trace into generated code and HCL
requirement: Each generated source file that permits comments must start with a header: the line `Generated by dsml <major>. Do not edit.`, then the line `Elements:` with the identities of its model elements in sorted order.

section: Trace into generated code and HCL
requirement: The generator must write the trace manifest `.dsml/trace.gen.json`. For each element, it must give each generated file, each symbol in that file (class, function, route or HCL resource address) and the line range of the symbol.

section: Trace into generated code and HCL
requirement: The trace manifest must give the HCL resource addresses of each infrastructure element, so a person can find the AWS resources of an element from its `dsml:element` tag or from its address.

section: Trace into generated code and HCL
requirement: The trace manifest must be sorted by element identity, then by file path, then by line.

A trace comment must be a line comment with the form `trace: <ID>[, <ID>]`: `# trace: R-001` in Python, HCL and YAML, and `// trace: R-001` in TypeScript. An ID can be a short name or a qualified name.
The toolchain must read trace comments in the hand-written files of the output folders and of the test folders in the configuration file. It must not read generated files for trace comments.
A trace comment applies to the next symbol in the file. If no symbol follows, it applies to the file.
The orphan report must list each trace comment with an ID that is not in the model.
`dsml trace` must write the four reports `coverage`, `orphans`, `impact` and `suspect` in the table of the section "Reports".

The coverage report must give each requirement one status: `missing` (no satisfying element), `satisfied` (a satisfying element, no verification) or `verified` (a satisfying element and a verification).
An element must count as changed if the hash of its IR form, with no source locations, is different from the hash in the baseline.
The `impact` and `suspect` reports must use the baseline that `--baseline` gives, or the default baseline that decision record 03 gives.
Each report must be available as HTML, CSV and JSON. The HTML report must be one file with no external resources.
Each report must give the model commit and the baseline commit, and no date or time.
